title: Take the planner's overrides, and name the ones that clash

blocks.text: Problem statement
With calendars in place, GridCap's vegetation planner started using the plan every week, and wrote:

Sometimes I know something the model doesn't. A crew is already on site near C17, so start it there in week 0. The county closes the road to C17 until October, so leave it. A landowner complained, so trim C02 first. I need to tell the planner these things and have it plan *around* them. And when it can't, "INFEASIBLE" is not an answer. Last week I forced in five circuits after a storm and got an empty plan and that one word. Tell me *which* of my decisions clash, in my words, so I know what to give up.

You start from the calendar scheduler of the lesson before. Take the planner's overrides: pin a trim to a crew and a first week, skip a circuit, or force one in, each with a reason. Refuse an override that names nothing before any model is built. When a season has no plan, name a smallest set of the planner's rules that clash (the musts, the budget and the overrides, never the physics of crews and weeks) in the planner's words, and print them in the report. Split the model out of `planner.py` into `model.py`, and the explanation into `explain.py`.

**The explanation.** Name the rules in the order they are made: each must as its circuit comes in the season, then the budget, then the overrides in the order given. The tests compare the explanation with an exact tuple in that order.

**The report.** After the crew lines, a plan with an explanation prints `these rules cannot all hold; change one of them:` and one line per rule, two spaces, `- ` and the rule's words. An INFEASIBLE plan has no trims: its status line reads `status INFEASIBLE: 0 trims, cost $0k, risk carried $0k`, and each crew's line shows only its weeks off.

**`main.py`.** After the tiny season's report it prints two more sections, each after an empty line. First the title `skip C03:` and the report of the tiny season with one override, `Override("skip", "C03", reason="road closed")`. Then the title `pin C01 and C05 a week apart on K1:` and the report with two, `Override("pin", "C01", crew="K1", start=12, reason="crew is nearby")` and `Override("pin", "C05", crew="K1", start=13, reason="landowner asked")`, which cannot both hold. Keep the line that sets `planner.WORKERS = 1`.
Run's report gains the two sections above, as `expected/report.txt` shows. Submit runs every test in `tests/`, the earlier steps' included, and compares Run's report with the expected one.
Blueprint
Write each method below. The tests check each one by itself and the whole program end to end, so you may change any other part of the code as you see fit.
`build` in `vegcrew/model.py`
def build(season: Season, overrides: tuple[Override, ...] = ()) -> TrimModel

items: **Contract.** The model of the lesson before, moved to model.py with crew_ids, horizon and start_domain, and built with the overrides. Every rule a planner can change sits behind a named literal, with its words: `must_<cid>` (`<cid> is overdue and must be trimmed this season`), budget (`the season's budget is $<budget>k`, the budget written with a thousands comma, as f"{budget:,}" writes it: `$962k`, `$1,000k`) and `override_<i>` (`override <i>: ` followed by the override's own words, as Override.says gives them: `trim <cid> on <crew> from week <start> (<reason>)` for a pin, `leave <cid> for next season (<reason>)`, `trim <cid> this season (<reason>)`, with `no reason given` when the reason is empty). A skip leaves its circuit untrimmed; a pin or force trims it; a pin also fixes the crew and the first week it names. The rules are made in this order: each must as its circuit comes in the season's order, then the budget, then the overrides in the order given.
**Modeling idea.** A rule behind a literal holds only when its literal is true, so the search can be asked which literals cannot all be true.

**Taught in** [4.4.2 Native Logic: `AddBoolOr`, `AddImplication`, `OnlyEnforceIf`](../../../../04-google-or-tools-in-depth/15-cpsat-core/units/unit-02/4.4.2-native-logic-addboolor-addimplication-onlyenforceif.unit.html).

"""The CP-SAT model of a season: every trim an optional interval on one crew, every planner's rule
behind a named literal so that a failed plan can say which rules clash."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model

from vegcrew.data import DEFER_WEEKS, WEEKS_PER_MONTH, Circuit, Override, Season


def crew_ids(season: Season) -> list[str]:
    return [f"K{k}" for k in range(1, season.crews + 1)]


def horizon(season: Season) -> int:
    return season.months * WEEKS_PER_MONTH


@dataclass
class TrimModel:
    model: cp_model.CpModel
    trimmed: dict[str, cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)                 # circuit
    present: dict[tuple[str, str], cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)    # (circuit, crew)
    start: dict[tuple[str, str], cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)
    work: dict[tuple[str, str], cp_model.IntervalVar] = field(default_factory=dict)
    end: dict[str, cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)                     # circuit
    carried: dict[str, cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)                 # circuit
    rules: dict[str, cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)                   # name -> literal
    says: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)                                # name -> words

    def rule(self, name: str, says: str) -> cp_model.IntVar:
        """A literal that switches one of the planner's rules on; the rows it guards hold only if it is 1."""
        self.rules[name] = self.model.new_bool_var(name)
        self.says[name] = says
        return self.rules[name]


def start_domain(c: Circuit, h: int) -> cp_model.Domain:
    """Every first week that keeps the trim inside one of the circuit's windows and the season."""
    windows = c.windows or ((0, h - 1),)
    return cp_model.Domain.from_intervals(
        [[first, min(last, h - 1) - c.weeks + 1] for first, last in windows
         if min(last, h - 1) - c.weeks + 1 >= first])


def build(season: Season, overrides: tuple[Override, ...] = ()) -> TrimModel:
    tm = TrimModel(cp_model.CpModel())
    h = horizon(season)
    deferred = h + DEFER_WEEKS                      # the end week of a circuit left for next season
    for c in season.circuits:
        t = tm.trimmed[c.cid] = tm.model.new_bool_var(f"t_{c.cid}")
        e = tm.end[c.cid] = tm.model.new_int_var_from_domain(
            cp_model.Domain.from_intervals([[c.weeks, h], [deferred, deferred]]), f"e_{c.cid}")
        starts = start_domain(c, h)
        options = [] if starts.is_empty() else crew_ids(season)    # no window fits it: no options
        for k in options:
            p = tm.present[c.cid, k] = tm.model.new_bool_var(f"p_{c.cid}_{k}")
            s = tm.start[c.cid, k] = tm.model.new_int_var_from_domain(starts, f"s_{c.cid}_{k}")   # window_c
            tm.work[c.cid, k] = tm.model.new_optional_fixed_size_interval_var(s, c.weeks, p, f"w_{c.cid}_{k}")
            tm.model.add(e == s + c.weeks).only_enforce_if(p)                        # ends_c,k
        tm.model.add(sum(tm.present[c.cid, k] for k in options) == t)               # once_c
        tm.model.add(e == deferred).only_enforce_if(~t)                              # waits_c
        if c.must:
            overdue = tm.rule(f"must_{c.cid}", f"{c.cid} is overdue and must be trimmed this season")
            tm.model.add(t == 1).only_enforce_if(overdue)                            # must_c
        table = [c.carried(week) for week in range(deferred + 1)]
        tm.carried[c.cid] = tm.model.new_int_var(0, table[-1], f"r_{c.cid}")
        tm.model.add_element(e, table, tm.carried[c.cid])                            # risk_c
    for k in crew_ids(season):
        off = [tm.model.new_fixed_size_interval_var(first, last - first + 1, f"off_{k}_{first}")
               for first, last in season.crew_off.get(k, ())]
        tm.model.add_no_overlap([w for (_, crew), w in tm.work.items() if crew == k] + off)   # crew_k
    tm.model.add(sum(c.cost * tm.trimmed[c.cid] for c in season.circuits) <= season.budget).only_enforce_if(
        tm.rule("budget", f"the season's budget is ${season.budget:,}k"))                # budget
    for i, o in enumerate(overrides, start=1):
        on = tm.rule(f"override_{i}", f"override {i}: {o.says()}")
        t = tm.trimmed[o.cid]
        if o.kind == "skip":
            tm.model.add(t == 0).only_enforce_if(on)                                 # override_i
            continue
        tm.model.add(t == 1).only_enforce_if(on)                                     # pin and force
        if o.crew and (o.cid, o.crew) in tm.present:
            tm.model.add(tm.present[o.cid, o.crew] == 1).only_enforce_if(on)
        if o.start is not None:
            tm.model.add(tm.end[o.cid] == o.start + season.circuit(o.cid).weeks).only_enforce_if(on)
    tm.model.minimize(sum(tm.carried.values()))
    return tm

from vegcrew.data import Override, season_from_dict
from vegcrew.generate import scenario
from vegcrew.planner import make_plan

SIZE, SEED = "tiny", 54


def show_overrides() -> None:
    """The plan with one override it keeps, then the rules named when two overrides clash."""
    season = season_from_dict(scenario(SIZE, SEED))
    kept = (Override("skip", "C03", reason="road closed"),)
    clash = (Override("pin", "C01", crew="K1", start=12, reason="crew is nearby"),
             Override("pin", "C05", crew="K1", start=13, reason="landowner asked"))
    for title, overrides in (("skip C03:", kept), ("pin C01 and C05 a week apart on K1:", clash)):
        print()
        print(title)
        print(format_plan(season, make_plan(season, overrides)))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    planner.WORKERS = 1                            # one search worker: the same plan every run
    main([SIZE, "--seed", str(SEED)])
    show_overrides()

"""Why a season has no plan: the planner's rules that cannot all hold together, in the planner's words.

Every rule a planner can change (a must, the budget, an override) sits behind a literal (model.py). The
search takes those literals as assumptions; when it proves the season infeasible, CP-SAT names a set of
assumptions that is enough for the proof, and a deletion filter shrinks it to a minimal one: drop each
rule in turn, and keep it out only if the rest still cannot hold.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model

from vegcrew.data import Override, Season
from vegcrew.model import TrimModel, build


def holds(tm: TrimModel, names: list[str]) -> bool:
    """Can these rules all hold at once? One worker, stopped at the first plan: only yes or no matters."""
    tm.model.clear_assumptions()
    tm.model.add_assumptions([tm.rules[n] for n in names])
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    solver.parameters.num_workers = 1
    solver.parameters.stop_after_first_solution = True
    return solver.solve(tm.model) != cp_model.INFEASIBLE


def conflict(tm: TrimModel) -> list[str]:
    """A minimal set of rule names that cannot all hold, or [] if every rule can."""
    names = list(tm.rules)
    tm.model.clear_assumptions()
    tm.model.add_assumptions([tm.rules[n] for n in names])
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    solver.parameters.num_workers = 1                  # assumptions need a single worker
    if solver.solve(tm.model) != cp_model.INFEASIBLE:
        return []
    by_index = {lit.index: n for n, lit in tm.rules.items()}
    core = [by_index[i] for i in solver.sufficient_assumptions_for_infeasibility()]
    for name in list(core):                            # deletion filter
        rest = [n for n in core if n != name]
        if not holds(tm, rest):
            core = rest
    return sorted(core, key=names.index)               # in the order the rules were made


def why_infeasible(season: Season, overrides: tuple[Override, ...] = ()) -> list[str]:
    tm = build(season, overrides)
    return [tm.says[n] for n in conflict(tm)]

"""The plan as the vegetation manager reads it: one line per crew, one letter per week."""

from __future__ import annotations

from vegcrew.data import Season
from vegcrew.model import crew_ids, horizon
from vegcrew.planner import Plan


def format_plan(season: Season, plan: Plan) -> str:
    lines = [f"season {season.name}: {len(season.circuits)} circuits, budget ${season.budget:,}k, "
             f"crews {season.crews}, weeks {horizon(season)}",
             f"status {plan.status}: {len(plan.trims)} trims, cost ${plan.cost:,}k, "
             f"risk carried ${plan.risk_carried:,}k"]
    for k in crew_ids(season):
        trims = sorted((t for t in plan.trims.values() if t.crew == k), key=lambda t: t.start)
        week = ["."] * horizon(season)
        for first, last in season.crew_off.get(k, ()):
            week[first:last + 1] = "x" * (last - first + 1)
        for t in trims:
            week[t.start:t.end] = t.cid[-1] * (t.end - t.start)
        lines.append(f"  {k} {''.join(week)}  " + " ".join(f"{t.cid}:{t.start}-{t.end - 1}" for t in trims))
    if plan.explanation:
        lines.append("these rules cannot all hold; change one of them:")
        lines += [f"  - {says}" for says in plan.explanation]
    return "\n".join(lines)

"""Turn a season into a plan: each trim is one crew's run of consecutive weeks, scheduled by CP-SAT
to carry the least risk, since a circuit's risk grows every week it waits."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model

from vegcrew.data import DEFER_WEEKS, WEEKS_PER_MONTH, Circuit, Override, Season

TIME_LIMIT = 10.0                                   # seconds
WORKERS = 4                                         # parallel search workers


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Trim:
    cid: str
    crew: str                                       # K1, K2, ...
    start: int                                      # first week, counted from 0
    end: int                                        # the week after the last: end - start = weeks


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Plan:
    status: str                                     # OPTIMAL, FEASIBLE, INFEASIBLE, UNKNOWN or MODEL_INVALID
    trims: dict[str, Trim] = field(default_factory=dict)
    cost: int = 0                                   # $k spent
    risk_removed: int = 0                           # $k a year of risk the trims remove
    risk_carried: int = 0                           # $k of risk carried until each circuit is trimmed
    explanation: tuple[str, ...] = ()               # stub for lesson 14.1.6


def crew_ids(season: Season) -> list[str]:
    return [f"K{k}" for k in range(1, season.crews + 1)]


def horizon(season: Season) -> int:
    return season.months * WEEKS_PER_MONTH


@dataclass
class TrimModel:
    model: cp_model.CpModel
    trimmed: dict[str, cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)                 # circuit
    present: dict[tuple[str, str], cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)    # (circuit, crew)
    start: dict[tuple[str, str], cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)
    work: dict[tuple[str, str], cp_model.IntervalVar] = field(default_factory=dict)
    end: dict[str, cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)                     # circuit
    carried: dict[str, cp_model.IntVar] = field(default_factory=dict)                 # circuit


def start_domain(c: Circuit, h: int) -> cp_model.Domain:
    """Every first week that keeps the trim inside one of the circuit's windows and the season."""
    windows = c.windows or ((0, h - 1),)
    return cp_model.Domain.from_intervals(
        [[first, min(last, h - 1) - c.weeks + 1] for first, last in windows
         if min(last, h - 1) - c.weeks + 1 >= first])


def build(season: Season) -> TrimModel:
    tm = TrimModel(cp_model.CpModel())
    h = horizon(season)
    deferred = h + DEFER_WEEKS                      # the end week of a circuit left for next season
    for c in season.circuits:
        t = tm.trimmed[c.cid] = tm.model.new_bool_var(f"t_{c.cid}")
        e = tm.end[c.cid] = tm.model.new_int_var_from_domain(
            cp_model.Domain.from_intervals([[c.weeks, h], [deferred, deferred]]), f"e_{c.cid}")
        starts = start_domain(c, h)
        options = [] if starts.is_empty() else crew_ids(season)    # no window fits it: no options
        for k in options:
            p = tm.present[c.cid, k] = tm.model.new_bool_var(f"p_{c.cid}_{k}")
            s = tm.start[c.cid, k] = tm.model.new_int_var_from_domain(starts, f"s_{c.cid}_{k}")   # window_c
            tm.work[c.cid, k] = tm.model.new_optional_fixed_size_interval_var(s, c.weeks, p, f"w_{c.cid}_{k}")
            tm.model.add(e == s + c.weeks).only_enforce_if(p)                        # ends_c,k
        tm.model.add(sum(tm.present[c.cid, k] for k in options) == t)               # once_c
        tm.model.add(e == deferred).only_enforce_if(~t)                              # waits_c
        if c.must:
            tm.model.add(t == 1)                                                     # must_c
        table = [c.carried(week) for week in range(deferred + 1)]
        tm.carried[c.cid] = tm.model.new_int_var(0, table[-1], f"r_{c.cid}")
        tm.model.add_element(e, table, tm.carried[c.cid])                            # risk_c
    for k in crew_ids(season):
        off = [tm.model.new_fixed_size_interval_var(first, last - first + 1, f"off_{k}_{first}")
               for first, last in season.crew_off.get(k, ())]
        tm.model.add_no_overlap([w for (_, crew), w in tm.work.items() if crew == k] + off)   # crew_k
    tm.model.add(sum(c.cost * tm.trimmed[c.cid] for c in season.circuits) <= season.budget)   # budget
    tm.model.minimize(sum(tm.carried.values()))
    return tm


def check_overrides(season: Season, overrides: tuple[Override, ...]) -> list[str]:
    """Stub for lesson 14.1.6."""
    return []


def make_plan(season: Season, overrides: tuple[Override, ...] = ()) -> Plan:
    """Choose the circuits to trim, the crew for each and its weeks: the least risk carried through the
    season and the wait for the next, within the budget, one crew per trim, one trim per crew at a time,
    every trim inside one of its circuit's windows and outside its crew's weeks off, every must trimmed."""
    tm = build(season)
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    solver.parameters.max_time_in_seconds = TIME_LIMIT
    solver.parameters.num_workers = WORKERS
    status = solver.status_name(solver.solve(tm.model))
    if status not in ("OPTIMAL", "FEASIBLE"):
        return Plan(status)
    trims = {}
    for (cid, k), p in tm.present.items():
        if solver.boolean_value(p):
            start = solver.value(tm.start[cid, k])
            trims[cid] = Trim(cid, k, start, start + season.circuit(cid).weeks)
    chosen = [season.circuit(cid) for cid in trims]
    return Plan(status, trims, cost=sum(c.cost for c in chosen), risk_removed=sum(c.risk for c in chosen),
                risk_carried=round(solver.objective_value))

"""The plan as the vegetation manager reads it: one line per crew, one letter per week."""

from __future__ import annotations

from vegcrew.data import Season
from vegcrew.planner import Plan, crew_ids, horizon


def format_plan(season: Season, plan: Plan) -> str:
    lines = [f"season {season.name}: {len(season.circuits)} circuits, budget ${season.budget:,}k, "
             f"crews {season.crews}, weeks {horizon(season)}",
             f"status {plan.status}: {len(plan.trims)} trims, cost ${plan.cost:,}k, "
             f"risk carried ${plan.risk_carried:,}k"]
    for k in crew_ids(season):
        trims = sorted((t for t in plan.trims.values() if t.crew == k), key=lambda t: t.start)
        week = ["."] * horizon(season)
        for first, last in season.crew_off.get(k, ()):
            week[first:last + 1] = "x" * (last - first + 1)
        for t in trims:
            week[t.start:t.end] = t.cid[-1] * (t.end - t.start)
        lines.append(f"  {k} {''.join(week)}  " + " ".join(f"{t.cid}:{t.start}-{t.end - 1}" for t in trims))
    return "\n".join(lines)
